test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Between a square of perimeter 44 cm and a circle of circumference 44 cm, which figure has a larger area and by how much?
solution:
Given:

Perimeter of the square = 44 cm

Perimeter of square = Circumference of the circle

Formula used:

Circumference of the circle = 2πr

Area of the circle = πr2 

Perimeter of square = 4 × side

Area of square = (side)²

Calculation:

Side of square = (44)/(4) = 11 cm

As, Perimeter of square = Circumference of the circle

⇒ 44 = 2πr 

⇒ r = 7 cm

Area of the circle = πr2 

⇒ Area of the circle = ((22)/(7)) × 72 = 154 cm²

And, Area of square = 11² = 121 cm²

Now, 154 > 121 

⇒ Area of Circle > Area of Square

Difference in area

= Area of Circle - Area of Square

= 154 - 121

= 33 cm²

∴ Area of the circle is larger by 33 cm².

Hence, the correct answer is option 1).
